question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 11 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 24 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 19 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity = LCM(11, 24, 19) = 5016 units

Combined efficiency = (5016 ÷ 11) + (5016 ÷ 24) + (5016 ÷ 19)

Combined efficiency = 456 + 209 + 264 = 929 units/hr

Time taken together = Total Capacity ÷ Combined efficiency = 5016 ÷ 929

Time taken together = 5 ³⁷¹/₉₂₉ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 5 ³⁷¹/₉₂₉ hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Time taken by pipe A = 11 hours

⇒ Time taken by pipe B = 24 hours

⇒ Time taken by pipe C = 19 hours

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Total Work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total work (capacity of the tank) be the LCM of 11, 24, and 19.

⇒ LCM(11, 24, 19) = 11 × 24 × 19 = 5016

⇒ Total efficiency when operating together = 456 + 209 + 264 = 929 units/hr

⇒ Time taken to fill the tank together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 5016 ÷ 929

⇒ Time taken = 5 ³⁷¹/₉₂₉ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 5 ³⁷¹/₉₂₉ hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours, then the part of the tank filled by the pipe in 1 hour is 1/x.

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank (positive efficiency), while an outlet pipe empties the tank (negative efficiency). The net work done is the algebraic sum of their combined efficiencies.

Time and Work LCM Method

The Total Work is practically assumed to be the LCM of individual completion times. The efficiency of each unit is then calculated as Total Work ÷ Time, helping avoid complex fraction calculations.
